In 1 minute

DC labor planning

Benjamin · Labor Planning Analyst

A retail chain's distribution center runs with 320 operators over two shifts and reaches 45 thousand orders a day at campaign peaks.

When it runs
Every day at 3 p.m. for the following day (D-1), with a weekly version on Friday at 10 a.m. for the following week (D-7); immediate rerun when the next day's order forecast changes by more than 15%
What it delivers in production
An adjusted roster for the next day by process and hour, with proposed reallocations and call-ins and their costs, approved by the DC manager and HR at 4 p.m. and then communicated to operators via WhatsApp.
Who decides
Proposes the roster; manager and HR approve
Effort
Calibrate on 90 days; 3 weeks in proposal mode
Set up5 steps · 8 ready files

Do this
  1. 1In Google Drive, create the folder
  2. 2Inside it, create Input and Output
  3. 3Leave both empty until the test

# DC staffing rules

## Shifts and arithmetic
- Shift 1: 6 a.m. to 2:20 p.m. (hours 06 to 13 of the forecast). Shift 2: 2 p.m. to 10:20 p.m. (hours 14 to 21).
- In the sample, 1 productivity unit = 1 order.
- Process need in the shift = orders in the shift's peak hour divided by productivity, rounded up.
- Scheduled after absenteeism = scheduled for the process in the shift x (1 - percentage for the day and shift), rounded down.

## Order of solution
1. Reallocation in the same shift, from a process with a positive balance, only for those with the skill on record. Zero cost.
2. Overtime: up to 2 h per day. Only a shift 1 operator scheduled in their own process, who stays until 4:20 p.m. and covers hours 14 and 15 of shift 2. Choose by the lowest hour bank balance.
3. Day laborer: whatever is left, through the agency, by the confirmation cutoff time.

## Limits and costs
- Hour bank: anyone with a balance above 30 h is not called in.
- callable = no or empty: not callable.
- Minimum rest between workdays: 11 h. Weekly rest: 1 day.
- Overtime: R$ 30.00 per hour. Day laborer: the agency's cost_per_day.

## Rules with no leeway
- Need and balance by the shift peak. E.g.: picking in shift 1, peak of 560 at 10 a.m.: 6 people against 5 after absenteeism (6 x 0.9 = 5.4), balance -1.
- Reallocation only with the skill. E.g.: OP-111 moves from packing to picking in shift 1; in shift 2 nobody in packing has the picking skill.
- Overtime by the lowest balance among the callable. E.g.: OP-105 (5 h) and OP-101 (10 h), 2 x 2 h x R$ 30 = R$ 120; day laborers only would be 2 x R$ 185 = R$ 370, discarded.
- Not callable by category, with no code and no individual reason. E.g.: 4 marked as not callable (1 with the field empty) and 1 with an hour bank above 30 h.
- Adjustment = reallocated + overtime + day laborers, divided by the scheduled headcount; early release does not count. All bands apply. E.g.: 3 of 18 = 16.7%, above 15%: DC manager, HR and the e-commerce lead.
- PROPOSAL with each operator's code: OP-111 reallocated from packing to picking in shift 1; OP-105 and OP-101 with 2 h of overtime.

## Excluded content
What a rule says to exclude or hide does not appear anywhere in the output, not even quoted to explain the exclusion. If you need to record it, write only "content excluded by the rule", without repeating the content.

## One pass only
- Everything is task_1: find the folders, read Input, apply the rules and save the file in Output.
- Do not build a plan with separate steps (locate, read, classify, write, save). A 1-task plan.

Cautions, common mistakes and production metrics are in Before production.

Before production

Cautions

No call-in, release or roster write happens without approval by the DC manager and HR, because a roster is a labor act and an error becomes a liability. The limits of the collective bargaining agreement and the law are hard constraints: no overtime above the daily limit, no breach of the rest period between shifts and no calling in someone on vacation. The reason for leave or a medical certificate is not included in the data read; the agent only receives 'not callable' by operator code. Reallocation between processes requires the recorded certification. The WMS stays at read-only access scope and the time clock system accepts writes only to the proposed roster field, released through Connector decisions.

Common mistakes

  • Rostering by the day's average orders without the hourly curve; the 4 p.m. to 7 p.m. peak before the carrier cutoff blows up.
  • Calling overtime before reallocating; eight idle people in receiving would solve half the shortfall in picking at zero cost.
  • Ignoring expected absenteeism by weekday and shift; Monday's roster arrives 10% short of what the paper says.
  • Forgetting the minimum rest between shifts for people who left late the previous day; a call-in that looked legal is not.

Metrics

MetricRangeSource
Overtime as a percentage of the DC's payrollfrom 11% to 6% to 8% in 4 monthsestimate based on the described routine
Idle people in picking on low-volume daysfrom about 60 to fewer than 20 a dayestimate based on the described routine
Average error of the calculated need per process in calibrationbelow 8%estimate based on the described routine

Sample production output

Fictional sample. Proposed roster for 2026-09-03 (Wednesday), generated at 3:02 p.m. Forecast: 38,400 orders (e-commerce 'home week' campaign, +28% over the Wednesday average). Draft for approval by the DC manager and HR. Process | Shift 1 (6 a.m.-2:20 p.m.) need / rostered after expected absenteeism (7%) | Shift 2 (2 p.m.-10:20 p.m.) need / rostered
Receiving | 22 / 30 (+8) | 14 / 18 (+4) || Picking | 118 / 96 (-22) | 132 / 101 (-31)
Packing | 44 / 40 (-4) | 51 / 42 (-9) || Shipping | 26 / 24 (-2) | 31 / 28 (-3)
HOURLY PEAK: picking between 4 p.m. and 7 p.m. needs 148 people for the 8 p.m. cutoff; a flat roster does not cover it.
PROPOSAL: reallocate 8 from receiving to picking on shift 1 and 4 on shift 2 (certification ok, zero cost) | call in 14 shift 1 operators for 2 h of overtime from 2:20 p.m. to 4:20 p.m. (hour bank, within the 2 h/day limit, rest between shifts respected, estimated cost R$ 1,960) | 18 day laborers for picking and packing on shift 2 (agency confirms by 4:30 p.m., cost R$ 4,680) | shipping: no action, 2 h of slack before the cutoff
NOT CALLABLE: 6 operators on vacation, 3 with a medical certificate, 5 with an hour bank balance above the limit, 4 who worked until 11 p.m. yesterday (rest between shifts).
TOTAL COST OF THE PROPOSAL: R$ 6,640 | alternative with overtime only: R$ 9,100 and breaks the daily limit for 7 operators, ruled out.
APPROVAL: DC manager and HR by 4 p.m.; call-in via WhatsApp after approval.
